papers.title: Adaptive Submodular Ranking and Routing
papers.abstract: We study a general stochastic ranking problem where an algorithm needs to adaptively select a sequence of elements so as to "cover" a random scenario (drawn from a known distribution) at minimum expected cost. The coverage of each scenario is captured by an individual submodular function, where the scenario is said to be covered when its function value goes above a given threshold. We obtain a logarithmic factor approximation algorithm for this adaptive ranking problem, which is the best possible (unless P=NP). This problem unifies and generalizes many previously studied problems with applications in search ranking and active learning. The approximation ratio of our algorithm either matches or improves the best result known in each of these special cases. Furthermore, we extend our results to an adaptive vehicle routing problem, where costs are determined by an underlying metric. This routing problem is a significant generalization of the previously-studied adaptive traveling salesman and traveling repairman problems. Our approximation ratio nearly matches the best bound known for these special cases. Finally, we present experimental results for some applications of adaptive ranking.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究自适应排序问题以最小化覆盖随机场景的期望成本。
summary_zh.method: 提出对数因子近似算法，结合子模函数和自适应选择。
summary_zh.result: 算法在多个特例中达到或改进已知最优比。
summary_zh.validation: 在搜索排序和主动学习应用中进行实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: This paper studies a general stochastic ranking problem to minimize expected cost of covering random scenarios with submodular functions.
summary_en.method: A logarithmic factor approximation algorithm is proposed for adaptive ranking, unifying and generalizing several previous problems.
summary_en.result: The approximation ratio matches or improves the best known results in various special cases.
summary_en.validation: Experimental results are presented for applications including search ranking and active learning.

papers.title: Stress partitioning behavior of an AlSi10Mg alloy produced by selective laser melting during tensile deformation using in situ neutron diffraction
papers.first_author_affiliation: Neutron Science Division, Korea Atomic Energy Research Institute, Daejeon 34057, South Korea

corresponding_authors.name: Wanchuck Woo
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Neutron Science Division, Korea Atomic Energy Research Institute, Daejeon 34057, South Korea

corresponding_authors.name: Shi-Hoon Choi
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Department of Printed Electronics Engineering, Sunchon National University, Sunchon 57922, South Korea

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了AlSi10Mg铝合金的选择性激光熔化及拉伸过程中的应力分配，与生物医用植入物的应力遮挡、疲劳等方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address porous structure, stress shielding, fatigue, or any biomedical context; it focuses on aluminum alloy for non-biomedical structural applications.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究SLM制备AlSi10Mg合金在拉伸时的应力分配行为
summary_zh.method: 使用原位中子衍射测量各相晶格应变，分析应力分配
summary_zh.result: 揭示了Al基体与Si共晶间的应力转移机制
summary_zh.validation: 通过原位中子衍射实验验证应力分配模型

summary_en.motivation: To understand the stress partitioning behavior between phases during tensile deformation of additively manufactured AlSi10Mg alloy.
summary_en.method: In situ neutron diffraction was used to measure lattice strains in individual phases during tensile testing of SLM-produced AlSi10Mg.
summary_en.result: The Al matrix and Si eutectic exhibited distinct load-sharing characteristics, with stress transfer from Al to Si upon plastic deformation.
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation via in situ neutron diffraction combined with tensile testing.
